title: A Giant Planet Vanished — and It Isn't Coming Back for Decades
summary:
For the first time, astronomers watched a giant planet vanish. The planet, a 'hot Jupiter' called TOI-2535 b, sits about 1,000 light-years from Earth. Instead, it wobbled out of view.

Astronomers first spotted TOI-2535 b in April 2019 using NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, known as TESS. The telescope finds planets by watching for tiny dips in a star's brightness when a planet passes in front of it. TOI-2535 b is a gas giant like Jupiter, but it hugs its star far more tightly than Mercury hugs our sun. Mercury takes 88 days to complete one orbit; TOI-2535 b needs just 8.25 days.

Over seven years of watching, researchers noticed something odd. The planet's crossings arrived as much as six hours earlier or later than predicted. Then, in March, the planet simply did not show up at all.

The researchers now believe TOI-2535 b has a close neighbor: another giant planet with a tilted orbit. The two planets tug on each other, wobbling like a pair of spinning tops until one tips out of line with Earth. Samuel Yee, a study co-author at the University of California, Los Angeles, called it the most extreme example researchers have seen. The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly, he said, that its transit disappeared while the team was watching.

The same kind of wobble shapes eclipses closer to home. The moon's orbit is tilted, so the moon, Earth, and sun line up only sometimes. Erik Petigura, a UCLA astrophysicist and study co-author, explained that if the moon's orbit lined up perfectly with Earth's, we would see an eclipse every month.

Based on their calculations, TOI-2535 b will not cross its star again for another 30 to 50 years. Its partner planet may appear sooner, once it emerges from behind its star.
why_it_matters: Watching a planet disappear in real time shows how planets shape each other's paths, and it gives astronomers a rare live look at the forces that move worlds around their stars.

keywords.explanation: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, used to measure huge distances in space.
A hot Jupiter is a giant planet like Jupiter that orbits very close to its star, so it is very hot.
A gas giant is a huge planet made mostly of gas, like Jupiter.
A transit is when a planet passes in front of its star, making the star look a little dimmer.
An astrophysicist is a scientist who studies stars, planets, and how the universe works.

background_read: Astronomers find planets beyond our solar system by watching stars: when a planet passes in front of its star, the star's light dips slightly.
Planets can tug on each other with gravity, and over time those tugs can slowly tilt or shift their orbits.
The moon's orbit is tilted too, which is why the moon, Earth, and sun only line up for an eclipse some of the time.
Because TOI-2535 b is so far away, astronomers can only study it by watching its star, so a missing crossing tells them something has changed.
